```{r}
Country_region <- read.csv("/Users/wenlanzhang/Downloads/PhD_UCL/Data/Oxford/all.csv")

Country_region
```

```{r}
migrations_file <- "/Users/wenlanzhang/Downloads/PhD_UCL/Data/Oxford/Migration/international_migration_flow.csv"
migrations <- read_csv(migrations_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

migrations <- migrations %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(country_from),
    !is.na(country_to),
    country_from != "",
    country_to != ""
  )
# migrations

# Get unique countries from migration data
countries_with_data <- migrations %>%
  select(country_from, country_to) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), values_to = "alpha.2") %>%
  distinct(alpha.2)
countries_with_data
```


```{r}
# world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
# world
```

```{r}
# Get world map (minimal columns)
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  select(iso_a2, name, geometry)


# Fill missing information for France
world <- world %>%
  mutate(
    iso_a2 = ifelse(name == "France" & iso_a2 == "-99", "FR", iso_a2),
  )

# Fill missing information for Norway
world <- world %>%
  mutate(
    iso_a2 = ifelse(name == "Norway" & iso_a2 == "-99", "NO", iso_a2),
  )


world <- world %>%
  mutate(
    iso_a2 = ifelse(name == "Kosovo" & iso_a2 == "-99", "XK", iso_a2),
  )


# Verify
world %>% filter(name %in% c("France", "Norway", 'Kosovo'))



# Join with country_region to get regions
world_region <- world %>%
  left_join(Country_region %>% select(alpha.2, region), by = c("iso_a2" = "alpha.2"))
world_region
```

```{r}
# 4. Mark which countries have migration data
world_region <- world_region %>%
  mutate(has_data = ifelse(iso_a2 %in% countries_with_data$alpha.2, "Yes", "No"))

```




```{r}
# 5. Define your custom palette
pal_nodes <- c('#F0C37E', '#AFDBF4', '#F2C2D8', '#12529A', '#b7a8cf')

# 6. Plot map, color by region using custom palette

# Only keep region info for countries with migration data
world_region_plot <- world_region %>%
  mutate(region_to_plot = ifelse(has_data == "Yes", region, NA))

# Plot
ggplot(world_region_plot) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = region_to_plot), color = "black", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_nodes, na.value = "gray90") +  # countries without migration data = gray
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Countries with Migration Data by Region",
    fill = "Region"
  )
```
